result.title: TILE: Bridging LLMs and Table Foundation Models for Tabular Learning with Strings
result.summary: Real-world tables are often heterogeneous, combining numerical features with free-form string columns. Table foundation models (TFMs) excel on numerical tables but require strings to be encoded numerically, while large language models (LLMs) hold semantic knowledge but are not designed for tabular predictions. Most existing bridges use LLMs as plug-in encoders for cell strings, yet how to extract representations effectively for tabular learning remains underexplored. We show that the interface between LLMs and tables matter as much as the LLM itself. Applied cell-wise, larger LLMs do not give better features. With our interface, the same LLMs improve steadily with size. TILE (Table-Interfaced LLM Embeddings) combines four ingredients: row serialization to provide cross-column context, intermediate-layer extraction to avoid layers specialized for next-token prediction, columnar pooling to remove mean pooling's length bias, and by-pass features to route numbers and categories past the LLM. Paired with TFMs, TILE sets a new state of the art for tables with strings. Across 100 datasets, it beats the strongest baseline on 89% of splits, with gains across 7 LLMs and 10 tabular learners, and ranks first on the 108-dataset STRABLE benchmark.

AI.brief_summary: TILE 研究如何为含字符串列的异构表格构造 LLM 表示，提出行序列化、取中间层、按列池化以及让数值与类别特征绕过 LLM 的旁路设计，再与表格基础模型结合，在 100 个数据集与 STRABLE 上取得领先。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「中间层而非末层抽取」与「旁路特征」两条接口经验，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的取层选择、池化方式及视觉旁路/模态捷径提供可核查的对照线索，但论文本身面向表格预测，未涉及视觉推理。
